title: Project structure and config
summary: Organise an Express project into small files and read settings from process.env with safe defaults.

quiz.q: Which split is common for an Express project?
options: app.js builds the app and exports it, server.js starts listening
One file per HTTP status code
A separate project for every route
quiz.explain: Keeping `app` separate from `listen` lets tests import the app without starting a real server, exactly like the exercises in this course.

quiz.q: Why keep a port number or secret key out of your source code?
options: Different machines need different values, and secrets must not be shared in code
Numbers are not allowed in JavaScript files
It makes the code run faster
quiz.explain: Your laptop, a test server and production all need different settings, and secrets pushed to a public repository can be stolen. Settings go in the environment.

quiz.q: The environment has no PORT variable. What does this print?
quiz.explain: An unset variable is `undefined`, which is falsy, so `||` picks the default 3000.

quiz.q: The environment sets PORT to 8080. What is the type of `process.env.PORT`?
quiz.explain: Environment variables are always strings. Convert with `Number(process.env.PORT)` when you need a number.

quiz.q: Put the lines in order for a server.js that loads the app and starts listening.
quiz.explain: Load the app, work out the port from the environment with a default, then start listening.

exercise.task:
In `app.js`, build a `config` object from environment variables with defaults, and expose it:

- `appName` comes from `process.env.APP_NAME`, default `Task Manager`.
- `port` comes from `process.env.PORT` converted to a number, default `3000`.
- `env` comes from `process.env.NODE_ENV`, default `development`.
- `GET /config` sends the config as JSON: `{ appName, port, env }`.

The checker sets `APP_NAME` to `Campus API` and leaves the other two unset. Leave `module.exports = app;` at the bottom.
hints: Read a variable with `process.env.NAME`. If it is missing the value is `undefined`, so `process.env.NAME || 'default'` gives a fallback.
Environment variables are strings, so for the port write `Number(process.env.PORT) || 3000`. Build the object once near the top and send it from the route.
